source.title: Sparse autoencoders reveal organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic in single-cell foundation models: a comparative atlas of Geneformer and scGPT

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE feature geometry and compares it with SVD to test superposition, using a different method and biological foundation models rather than the original toy networks.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports perturbation-response and biological annotation results. Only results bearing on superposition, feature geometry, or SAE features as representational units are recorded here.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs on residual streams of two single-cell transformer foundation models (Geneformer, scGPT). It reports reconstruction, biological annotation and causal ablation of the recovered sparse features. That is V4-type evidence (real models contain sparse features an SAE can recover) in a new, non-LLM setting. No small toy networks are studied, so V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors claim SAEs reveal massive superposition (99.8% of features invisible to SVD, at least 82,525 concepts in 1,152 dims). Also add that they find feature-level causal specificity in Geneformer, but only 6.2% TF-regulatory specificity, which they attribute to the model rather than the SAE training data.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs on residual-stream activations of biological foundation models and compares decoder features with SVD; it does not reproduce the original toy-network construction or its sparsity and importance sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and layer: Geneformer and scGPT differ in reconstruction and feature statistics; Geneformer feature persistence falls sharply with depth; causal patching differs between models, and scGPT patching uses proxy expression values.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE decoder directions in both models have low pairwise cosine (|cos| 0.033–0.049, signed mean 0.0007), which the authors read as a geometric signature of superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary directions learned on real-model activations are nearly orthogonal, beyond what random directions in the same dimension would give.

record.problems: The study tests one SAE configuration (4× expansion, k=32); the original toy-network sparsity and importance transitions are not tested. Cross-layer feature matching does not establish run-to-run stability, completeness, or canonicality. scGPT causal patching uses proxy expression values, which the authors say may weaken the test.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing directly on the listed claim versions were left out.

untested.parts: All of V1: no small toy networks, no sparsity or importance sweep, no phase transition, no regular geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity and capacity competition are not measured.
No LLMs studied; neuron-level spread of features is not measured; only one SAE configuration (4×, k=32) is used.
Completeness, run-to-run stability and canonicality across dictionary sizes are not tested.
No test of multi-dimensional versus 1-D features.

missing.what: Annotation rates: 52.4% of Geneformer features and 31.0% of scGPT features annotated; novel (non-SVD) features 52.5% versus SVD-aligned 14.3%.
scGPT SAE variance explained 85.7–93.5% (mean 90.2%); 49 dead features in total.

record.verdict_notes: The study's superposition claims rest mainly on by-construction quantities: dictionary size, top-50 SVD comparison, and the cross-layer summed compression ratio. The study gives no random-direction baseline for the cosine statistics. These models are gene-token transformers, not LLMs, hence T3. Rows r1–r3 were mislinked to V1 and r5–r7 to V6.

versions.untested_parts: No small toy networks, sparsity sweep, importance sweep, or regular-geometry transition is tested; the models are biological foundation models and the SAE sparsity is fixed at k=32.
Neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, and dedicated dimensions for important features are not tested.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Geneformer and scGPT are single-cell foundation models, not LLMs; the study does not measure feature spread across neurons in LLMs.
Cross-layer persistence and causal effects of selected SAE features are examined, but completeness, reproducibility across SAE runs, and canonicality across alternative dictionaries are not tested.
The study measures SAE decoder-vector geometry, but does not compare against an alternative representation in which features are intrinsically multidimensional.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Counted alive SAE features across all layers and compared the atlas size with the model's hidden dimension.
rows.measure: Alive SAE feature count and stated compression relative to hidden dimensions
rows.value: 82,525 alive features across 18 layers; the paper describes this as at least 82,525 biological concepts in 1,152 dimensions and a compression ratio exceeding 70×.
rows.note: The feature total aggregates layer-specific dictionaries; the paper itself characterizes this as massive superposition.
rows.check: Mislinked to V1, which concerns small toy networks. The alive count is fixed by design (a 4× dictionary with almost all features alive), so it cannot show superposition. The '>70× compression' divides a total summed over 18 layers by one layer's width; the per-layer ratio is 4×.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder vectors with the top-50 SVD axes at each layer.
rows.measure: Fraction of SAE features aligned with a top-50 SVD axis
rows.value: 189 of 82,525 features (0.2%) aligned; 99.8% were classified as novel/invisible to this SVD comparison.
rows.note: SVD alignment is the study's operational comparison for whether SAE features are captured by standard linear decomposition.
rows.check: Mislinked to V1. Comparing 4,608 decoder directions against only the top-50 SVD axes makes about 99% non-alignment near-inevitable by construction. No baseline (e.g. random directions) is given.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Compared activation variance explained by SAEs and top-50 SVD axes.
rows.value: SAEs: 77–85%; the paper reports a 2.4× ratio versus top-50 SVD.
rows.note: The reported comparison supports the paper's claim that the SAE dictionary captures structure not represented by the top SVD axes.
rows.check: Mislinked to V1. The SAE recovers 77–85% of variance, so a substantial share goes unexplained. The SVD comparison is not matched: 32 active of 4,608 latents versus 50 axes.

source_check.correct: state=observed for V4: sparse dictionaries recover substantial activation structure. Unexplained variance does not make this existential recovery claim partial; V4 does not require complete reconstruction.
source_check.locator_found: Section 2.2 reports 77–85% SAE variance explained versus 31–38% for top-50 SVD; Section 2.1 reports biological annotation.
source_check.problem: The partial state imports a completeness requirement absent from V4.

rows.subject: scGPT whole-human
rows.size_stated: 12 layers, d=512; parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Counted alive SAE features across all layers.
rows.note: This is a cross-model extension of the feature-atlas result; the paper does not report an scGPT SVD comparison.
rows.check: Mislinked to V1. The feature count is set by dictionary size (2,048/layer). scGPT reconstruction (85.7–93.5%) and annotation (31%) are the informative results but are not recorded.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarities between SAE decoder vectors and compared within- versus between-module geometry.
rows.measure: Pairwise cosine similarity and within- versus between-module separation
rows.value: Mean pairwise cosine similarity = 0.0007; within-module versus between-module Cohen's d = 0.075.
rows.note: The study interprets the decoder-vector geometry as quasi-orthogonal; SAE features are represented by decoder directions.
rows.check: Decoder cosine statistics say nothing about 1-D versus multi-dimensional features (V6). A signed mean cosine near 0 is expected for any spread of directions. The authors note it is quasi-orthogonal 'by design'.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean absolute pairwise cosine between decoder vectors by layer.
rows.note: This is a separate absolute-cosine statistic from the signed mean pairwise cosine reported in Section 2.13.
rows.check: Does not test V6. The study gives no random baseline; random unit vectors in d=1152 give mean |cos| ≈0.024, so 0.033–0.040 is only slightly above chance.

rows.subject: scGPT whole-human
rows.size_stated: 12 layers, d=512; parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean absolute pairwise cosine between decoder vectors by layer.
rows.note: The decoder vectors are one direction per SAE feature; the study does not test alternative multidimensional feature representations.
rows.check: Does not test V6. For d=512, random unit vectors give mean |cos| ≈0.035; the reported 0.038–0.049 is near chance.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Tracked layer-0 features by decoder-vector cosine similarity against features in later layers.
rows.measure: Persistence of layer-0 SAE features across layers
rows.value: 114 matches at L1 (2.5%), 67 at L4 (1.5%), 10 at L8 (0.2%), 1 at L10 (approximately 0%), and 0 at L12 and later; the text reports no layer-0 feature survives past L11.
rows.note: The paper concludes that features are overwhelmingly layer-specific. This tests cross-layer persistence, not reproducibility across SAE runs or completeness of the atlas.
rows.check: Matching features across separately trained per-layer SAEs mixes genuine layer change with dictionary run variability. It does not test stability or canonicality of one dictionary, so it cannot show whether V5 holds.

rows.subject: Geneformer V2-316M
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed one SAE feature at layer 11, decoded the modified activation, and continued the forward pass.
rows.measure: Ratio of target-gene to other-gene logit disruption
rows.baseline: No feature ablation; numeric baseline not stated.
rows.value: Median specificity ratio 2.36×; 30/50 features (60%) exceeded 2× and 6/50 (12%) exceeded 10×.
rows.note: Selected feature ablations produced target-specific effects, but this does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units.
rows.check: Bears on whether the recovered sparse features are functionally real (V4), not on completeness or canonicality (V5). 30/50 features exceeded 2× specificity; 40% did not. The 50 features were selected as richly annotated.

source_check.correct: state=observed as positive functional evidence for recovered sparse features under V4. Median specificity is 2.36×; 30/50 exceed 2× and 6/50 exceed 10×. The remaining 20/50 do not exceed 2×.
source_check.problem: Mixed causal specificity does not make V4 partial: V4 does not require every recovered feature to pass a causal-specificity threshold.

rows.subject: scGPT whole-human
rows.size_stated: 12 layers, d=512; parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Performed the same single-feature causal patching experiment at layer 7.

conditions.value: proxy expression values; uniform 1.0 for all genes

rows.baseline: 1× would indicate equal target and off-target disruption.
rows.value: Median specificity 0.98×; mean 1.02×; 0/50 features exceeded 2× specificity.
rows.note: The authors say proxy expression values may explain the weaker causal signal.
rows.check: Median specificity 0.98×, 0/50 features above 2×. The authors attribute this to proxy input values (uniform 1.0), so the test is confounded.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V4 from this measure. Causal specificity is absent under the proxy-input intervention: median 0.98×, mean 1.02×, 0/50 above 2×. This does not establish absent sparse-feature recovery.
source_check.locator_found: Section 2.7, scGPT causal patching paragraph; Section 2.3 separately reports successful sparse reconstruction and annotation.
source_check.problem: Absent causal specificity is conflated with absence of the sparse representations named by V4.

relationships.condition: Geneformer V2-316M, all 18 layers, TopK 4×, k=32
relationships.reason: SAEs reconstruct 77–85% of variance (r3). Ablating selected L11 features gives median 2.36× target-specific disruption (r9). Text: 52.4% of features annotate to ontologies. Non-LLM setting.
relationships.display_finding: SAEs reconstructed 77–85% of variance, and ablating selected layer-11 features gave a median 2.36× target-specific disruption. 52.4% of features annotated to ontologies, in a non-language setting.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Geneformer V2-316M, all 18 layers, TopK 4×, k=32
source_check.reason: r3 demonstrates substantial sparse reconstruction; r9 supplies positive functional evidence for selected recovered features. Section 2.1 reports 52.4% ontology annotation. This supports the recovery claim in a biological transformer setting.

relationships.condition: Geneformer feature-level evidence that depends on construction choices
relationships.reason: Counts and SVD non-alignment follow from dictionary size and top-50 SVD choice (r1, r2). 40% of selected features fall below 2× causal specificity (r9). Unexplained variance is 15–23% (r3).
relationships.display_finding: The number of features and the lack of SVD alignment followed from the chosen dictionary size and top-50 SVD. Also, 40% of selected features fell below 2× causal specificity, and 15–23% of variance stayed unexplained.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Geneformer feature-level evidence that depends on construction choices
source_check.reason: r1–r2 cannot establish superposition from feature counts or non-alignment alone, but weak diagnostics do not demonstrate a boundary of V4. Construction choices were not varied. Incomplete reconstruction and heterogeneous causal specificity do not contradict V4, which requires neither completeness nor universal causal specificity.

relationships.condition: scGPT whole-human, layer-7 causal patching with proxy inputs
relationships.reason: 0/50 features exceeded 2× specificity (median 0.98×), so recovered features showed no causal specificity here; the authors attribute this to proxy expression inputs (r10).
relationships.display_finding: None of 50 features exceeded 2× causal specificity (median 0.98×), and the authors attribute this to proxy expression inputs.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: scGPT whole-human, layer-7 causal patching with proxy inputs
source_check.reason: r10 tests causal specificity under proxy inputs, not whether sparse features can be recovered. Section 2.3 reports successful scGPT reconstruction and annotation. The suggested proxy-input explanation is not experimentally isolated.

relation.reason: Its own results bear on recoverable sparse representations in real transformer models, extending V4 to a biological setting.

tranche.reason: The study extends sparse-feature recovery analyses to biological foundation models and reports reconstruction, annotation, and intervention results.

source_check.notes: The 82,525 total aggregates 18 separate layer dictionaries; dividing it by one layer's 1,152 dimensions does not establish simultaneous representational capacity. Methods 5.6 replaces hidden states with SAE reconstructions during ablation; no reconstruction-only intervention control is stated.

statements.correction: Geneformer: 30/50 selected annotated features exceeded 2× specificity; 20/50 did not exceed 2×. scGPT: 0/50 exceeded 2×; median 0.98× under uniform 1.0 proxy expression inputs. V4 does not require causal specificity.
statements.problem: The causal-specificity results are accurate, but they do not independently limit V4's sparse-recovery claim. Also, 30/50 exceeding 2× establishes that 40% did not exceed it, rather than strictly fell below it.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The atlas contains 82,525 alive features, 99.8% not aligned with the top-50 SVD axes, with SAE variance explained of 77–85% versus 31–38% for SVD (r1–r3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study finds 24,527 alive SAE features across 12 layers and describes the cross-model result as massive superposition, although it does not report an SVD comparison for scGPT (r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Layer-0 features have few matches in adjacent layers and none at L12 or later, qualifying any account of SAE features as stable model-wide units; run-to-run stability and completeness remain untested (r8).
